papers.title: UniCoracle: Automated hierarchical Feature Selection via Bottom-Up Propagation and Top-Down Skimming using the UniCorP algorithm and the Coracle machine-learning framework
papers.summary: Abstract Identifying meaningful associations between microbial communities and measured physiological or environmental variables becomes increasingly complex and computationally demanding given the continuous growth of microbiome datasets. The Coracle machine learning (ML) framework was recently developed to address this by integrating multiple data transformations, feature selection techniques, and ML models to yield condensed lists of features that align to target variables of interest. Further, we recently developed the UniCorP feature aggregation algorithm to identify uniquely correlated features (UNICORNs) based on the UniCor metric that iteratively enrich each taxonomic level in an automated bottom-up approach. Here we present UniCoracle, a fully automated analytical framework that integrates UniCorP’s bottom-up propagation approach with a subsequent and newly developed top-down skimming (TDS) strategy, implemented with the Coracle ML framework. This combined approach leverages the inherent taxonomic structure of microbiome community data (e.g., ASVs derived from 16S rRNA gene amplicon sequencing) to maintain predictive stability, reduce computational runtime, and identify biologically meaningful taxonomic associations. We compare the original, non-hierarchical Coracle with the TDS Coracle method and the UniCoracle approach. Evaluations across the tested datasets show that UniCoracle achieves competitive or improved predictive performance relative to both Coracle’s multi-step and the TDS-based Coracle implementations. Our results demonstrate UniCoracle’s improvements in predictive accuracy over both Coracle’s multi-step and the TDS Coracle methods. UniCoracle provides full control over feature set size and runtime, offering a streamlined and user-friendly framework for biological hypothesis generation. It identifies features (e.g., bacterial taxa) at the lowest (most specific) hierarchical level (e.g., ASV or species within a taxonomic hierarchy) that are associated with continuous target variables. Availability: UniCoracle is freely accessible via a dedicated web server at micportal.org. The source code is open-source and available on GitHub at github.com/SebastianStaab/UniCoracle.git and Zenodo at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.19050205

papers.llm_research_question_zh: 随着微生物组数据集的持续增长，确定微生物群落与各种生理或环境变量之间的有意义关联变得越来越复杂，同时也需要耗费更多的计算资源。
llm_highlights_zh: 最近，人们开发了Coracle机器学习框架来解决这一问题。该框架通过整合多种数据转换方法、特征选择技术以及机器学习模型，能够生成与目标变量相匹配的精简特征列表。
此外，我们最近开发了UniCorP特征聚合算法，该算法基于UniCor指标来识别那些具有独特关联性的特征，并通过自下而上的自动化方法逐步丰富各个分类层次的特征信息。
在这里，我们介绍UniCoracle——这一完全自动化的分析框架。它将UniCorP的自下而上的传播算法与随后新开发的自上而下的扫描策略相结合，并通过Coracle机器学习框架得以实现。
papers.llm_rss_summary_zh: 摘要：随着微生物组数据集规模的持续增长，识别微生物群落与生理或环境变量之间的关联变得越来越复杂，同时也对计算资源提出了更高的要求。为此，我们最近开发了Coracle机器学习框架——该框架通过整合多种数据转换技术、特征选择方法及机器学习模型，能够生成与目标变量相匹配的特征列表。此外，我们还设计了UniCorP特征聚合算法，该算法基于“UniCor”指标，采用自下而上的迭代方式来识别那些具有独特相关性的特征。本文所介绍的UniCoracle是一个完全自动化的分析框架：它将UniCorP的自下而上分析方法与后来开发的自上而下的筛选策略相结合，并通过Coracle机器学习框架加以实现。这种结合方式充分利用了微生物组数据本身的分类结构（例如通过16S rRNA基因扩增子测序获得的ASV信息），从而确保预测结果的稳定性、降低计算成本，并帮助识别具有生物学意义的分类关联。通过对多个测试数据集的评估，我们发现UniCoracle在预测性能上优于传统的多步骤分析方法或基于TDS策略的分析方案；其结果进一步证明了UniCoracle在预测准确性方面的优势。该框架允许用户完全控制特征集的大小及计算耗时，为生物假设的生成提供了高效且易于使用的工具。它能够识别出那些与连续型目标变量存在关联的特征——这些特征通常位于分类体系的最低层级（例如ASV或特定物种）。UniCoracle可通过micportal.org网站免费获取；其源代码已开源，可在GitHub（github.com/SebastianStaab/UniCoracle.git）及Zenodo平台（https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.19050205）上下载。

papers.primary_summary_raw: Identifying meaningful associations between microbial communities and measured physiological or environmental variables becomes increasingly complex and computationally demanding given the continuous growth of microbiome datasets. The Coracle machine learning (ML) framework was recently developed to address this by integrating multiple data transformations, feature selection techniques, and ML models to yield condensed lists of features that align to target variables of interest. Further, we recently developed the UniCorP feature aggregation algorithm to identify uniquely correlated features (UNICORNs) based on the UniCor metric that iteratively enrich each taxonomic level in an automated bottom-up approach. Here we present UniCoracle, a fully automated analytical framework that integrates UniCorP's bottom-up propagation approach with a subsequent and newly developed top-down skimming (TDS) strategy, implemented with the Coracle ML framework. This combined approach leverages the inherent taxonomic structure of microbiome community data (e.g., ASVs derived from 16S rRNA gene amplicon sequencing) to maintain predictive stability, reduce computational runtime, and identify biologically meaningful taxonomic associations. We compare the original, non-hierarchical Coracle with the TDS Coracle method and the UniCoracle approach. Evaluations across the tested datasets show that UniCoracle achieves competitive or improved predictive performance relative to both Coracle's multi-step and the TDS-based Coracle implementations. Our results demonstrate UniCoracle's improvements in predictive accuracy over both Coracle's multi-step and the TDS Coracle methods. UniCoracle provides full control over feature set size and runtime, offering a streamlined and user-friendly framework for biological hypothesis generation. It identifies features (e.g., bacterial taxa) at the lowest (most specific) hierarchical level (e.g., ASV or species within a taxonomic hierarchy) that are associated with continuous target variables. Availability: UniCoracle is freely accessible via a dedicated web server at micportal.org. The source code is open-source and available on GitHub at github.com/SebastianStaab/UniCoracle.git and Zenodo at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.19050205. Supplementary information: Example datasets and a tutorial are provided on the web server: micportal.org.

papers.title: Structural-information Guided Fusion for spatial domain identification from Spatial Transcriptomics
papers.summary: Abstract Motivation Accurate spatial domain identification is essential for understanding tissue organization and pathological mechanisms in spatial transcriptomics. However, existing methods mainly rely on expression profiles and spatial coordinates. Intercellular interactions are often overlooked. At the same time, preserving both local neighborhood continuity and global topological structure remains difficult. Results We propose SGFST (Structural-information Guided Fusion for spatial domain identification from Spatial Transcriptomics), a novel framework for spatial domain identification in spatial transcriptomics. SGFST integrates a spatial graph and a signal graph, and employs a dual-branch graph convolutional network with attention-based fusion to capture complementary spatial and functional information. In addition, SGFST jointly optimizes a Bayesian personalized ranking loss, a zero-inflated negative binomial loss, and a distance structural information constraint to preserve local neighborhood continuity, reconstruct expression signals, and maintain global topological consistency. Experimental results on multiple datasets demonstrate that SGFST outperforms several state-of-the-art methods in spatial domain identification. Availability and implementation The code of SGFST is available at Github ( https://github.com/xkmaxidian/SGFST ) and Zenodo(DOI : 10.5281/zenodo.20624899)

papers.llm_rss_summary_zh:
**摘要**  
在空间转录组学中，准确识别组织结构与病理机制所依赖的空间域信息至关重要。然而现有方法主要依赖于表达谱数据及空间坐标信息，往往忽视了细胞间的相互作用；同时，在保持局部邻域连续性与全局拓扑结构之间的平衡也面临挑战。  

**研究结果**  
我们提出了SGFST这一新型框架，用于解决空间转录组学中的空间域识别问题。该框架整合了空间图与信号图，并采用基于注意力机制的双分支图卷积网络来融合这两种信息，从而有效捕捉空间与功能层面的互补特征。此外，SGFST还结合了贝叶斯个性化排序损失函数、零膨胀负二项式损失函数以及距离结构信息约束条件，以同时实现局部邻域连续性的保持、表达信号的重建以及全局拓扑结构的统一性。多项实验数据表明，SGFST在空间域识别方面的性能显著优于现有先进方法。  

**代码与资源**  
SGFST的源代码可在Github（https://github.com/xkmaxidian/SGFST）及Zenodo平台（DOI：10.5281/zenodo.20624899）上获取。

papers.title: ReGAIN: A bioinformatics platform for assessing probabilistic co-occurrence between resistance genes in bacterial pathogens
papers.summary: Abstract Motivation Multidrug-resistant bacterial pathogens continue to rise globally, yet scalable methods are needed to infer how resistance determinants co-occur across pathogen populations and to quantify conditional dependencies underlying co-occurrence and shared genetic context. Results We present ReGAIN (Resistance Gene Association and Inference Network), an open-source framework that applies Bayesian network structure learning to infer probabilistic, conditional dependency relationships among antibiotic resistance, heavy metal tolerance, stress response, and virulence determinants in bacteria. In contrast to pairwise co-occurrence analyses, ReGAIN reports conditional probabilities, relative risks, and absolute risk differences with confidence intervals to prioritize candidate relationships for downstream prioritization. Applied across ESKAPEE pathogens, ReGAIN recapitulated established resistance gene relationships and identified additional candidate patterns consistent with co-selection and shared genetic context. Together, these results support scalable, reproducible population-wide analysis of resistance networks for surveillance, comparative genomics and epidemiology. Availability ReGAIN analyses are performed using Python v3.11.5 and R v4.4.1 and is available as open-source software through Bioconda at {{ https://anaconda.org/bioconda/regain-cli }}. Source code and documentation can be found at {{ https://github.com/ERBringHorvath/regain_CLI }}. All genomes used in this publication were downloaded from the National Center for Biotechnology Information database. Large supplementary tables and results data from the ESKAPEE pathogen example network analyses can be downloaded from https://figshare.com/articles/dataset/ReGAIN_command_line_software_and_supplemental_figures_/28959431

多重耐药细菌病原体在全球范围内持续增加，因此亟需可行的方法来研究这些耐药性决定因子在病原体群体中的共现规律，并量化其共现现象背后的条件依赖关系及共同遗传背景。

papers.primary_summary_raw:
MOTIVATION: Multidrug-resistant bacterial pathogens continue to rise globally, yet scalable methods are needed to infer how resistance determinants co-occur across pathogen populations and to quantify conditional dependencies underlying co-occurrence and shared genetic context.

RESULTS: We present ReGAIN (Resistance Gene Association and Inference Network), an open-source framework that applies Bayesian network structure learning to infer probabilistic, conditional dependency relationships among antibiotic resistance, heavy metal tolerance, stress response, and virulence determinants in bacteria. In contrast to pairwise co-occurrence analyses, ReGAIN reports conditional probabilities, relative risks, and absolute risk differences with confidence intervals to prioritize candidate relationships for downstream prioritization. Applied across ESKAPEE pathogens, ReGAIN recapitulated established resistance gene relationships and identified additional candidate patterns consistent with co-selection and shared genetic context. Together, these results support scalable, reproducible population-wide analysis of resistance networks for surveillance, comparative genomics and epidemiology.

AVAILABILITY: ReGAIN analyses are performed using Python v3.11.5 and R v4.4.1 and is available as open-source software through Bioconda at {{https://anaconda.org/bioconda/regain-cli}}. Source code and documentation can be found at {{https://github.com/ERBringHorvath/regain_CLI}}. All genomes used in this publication were downloaded from the National Center for Biotechnology Information database. Large supplementary tables and results data from the ESKAPEE pathogen example network analyses can be downloaded from https://figshare.com/articles/dataset/ReGAIN_command_line_software_and_supplemental_figures_/28959431.

SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION: Supplementary data are available at Bioinformatics online.

papers.title: LoMuS: Low-Rank Adaptation with Sequence Multi-representation Improves Protein Stability Prediction
papers.summary: Abstract Motivation Protein folding stability is a key determinant for understanding protein dynamics, including molecular function, pathogenicity, and protein engineering. Yet, accurate prediction of protein stability remains challenging due to high variability in available data, particularly when only sequence information is available and structural knowledge is limited or unavailable. In this work, we introduce LoMuS, a multi-representation-based deep learning model that predicts dataset-provided protein stability scores directly from the primary sequence. In the core of the model architecture, a fusion network integrates explicit physicochemical descriptors with low-rank adapted protein language model derived embeddings from the sequence that consistently gains across standard experimental stability benchmarks. Results We rigorously evaluate LoMuS across multiple settings, such as absolute folding stability scoring, mutation landscape stability scoring, held-out protein domains, out-of-distribution label regimes, and per-protein evaluation. LoMuS consistently outperforms sequence-only baselines, achieving an absolute performance gain of at least 10% in Spearman’s rank correlation across several benchmarks. Per-protein evaluations further demonstrate robust performance gains. Ablation analyses confirm that complementary signals from physicochemical descriptors and sequence embeddings are critical to the effectiveness of the proposed multi-representation approach. We believe LoMuS advances protein engineering research by improving the prediction and ranking of protein stability scores. Availability All codes including data preparation scripts, training and validation recipes, and experimental configurations for LoMuS are available at: https://github.com/kabir-ai2bio-lab/LoMuS

papers.llm_rss_summary_zh:
**摘要与动机**  
蛋白质的折叠稳定性是理解其动态行为、分子功能、致病性以及进行蛋白质工程设计的关键因素。然而，由于现有数据存在较大变异性——尤其是在仅掌握序列信息而结构信息有限或无法获取的情况下——准确预测蛋白质稳定性仍然面临挑战。在本研究中，我们提出了LoMuS这一基于多表示学习的深度学习模型，该模型能够直接根据蛋白质的初级序列来预测实验测得的稳定性数值。在模型架构的核心部分，融合网络将明确的物理化学描述符与从序列中提取的低维嵌入信息相结合，而这些嵌入信息在各种标准的稳定性评估指标中均表现出优异的性能。  

**实验结果**  
我们通过多种测试场景对LoMuS进行了严格评估，包括绝对折叠稳定性评分、突变位点对稳定性的影响分析、针对特定蛋白质结构域的预测能力测试，以及在不同数据分布条件下的性能表现。结果表明，LoMuS在各项测试中均显著优于仅依赖序列信息的传统模型，在多个评估指标上的性能提升幅度至少达到了10%。进一步的研究还证实，物理化学描述符与序列嵌入信息之间的互补作用是该模型高效预测蛋白质稳定性的关键因素。我们相信，LoMuS的问世将为蛋白质工程研究带来重要进展。

papers.title: Cross-dataset annotation harmonization for cell-type hierarchy construction
papers.summary: Abstract Motivation Single-cell transcriptomic datasets annotate cell types with diverse schemes and varying resolution. This poses challenges in building unified hierarchical cell-type structures and hinders integration of large-scale datasets. To address this, several computational methods have been developed to harmonize cell type annotations across datasets and build data-driven hierarchies of cell types. Results Here, we benchmarked three state-of-the-art methods: scHPL, treeArches and CellHint. We evaluated these methods across 5 simulated scenarios and 5 real-world scenarios across cell types and organs. To assess harmonization results, we designed three metrics, Annotation Harmonization F1-score (AH-F1), Tree Edit Distance Similarity (TEDS) and Parent-Children Branches Similarity (PCBS), comparing the constructed cell-type hierarchies and the knowledge-based ones. Based on the benchmarking results, we found that methods performed well in simulated scenarios but still have room for improvement in complex real-world data. Thus, we developed OTHarmonizer, a tool based on partial optimal transport (OT) for cell-type harmonization and hierarchy construction. OTHarmonizer excels in accurately capturing equivalent and hierarchical relationships between cell types, offering a more effective approach for the cell-type hierarchy construction across datasets. Availability and Implementation The simulated and real-world datasets in the benchmark are available on https://figshare.com/articles/dataset/OTHarmonizer/28243205 . The source codes for the benchmark and OTHarmonizer are available online on GitHub at https://github.com/Duck-Boss/OTHarmonizer

**摘要与动机**  
单细胞转录组数据集采用多种不同的方案对细胞类型进行标注，且这些方案的分辨率各不相同。这种差异给构建统一的细胞类型层次结构带来了挑战，也阻碍了大规模数据集的整合与应用。为解决这一问题，人们开发了一系列计算方法，旨在协调不同数据集中的细胞类型标注信息，并建立基于数据的细胞类型层次体系。  

**研究结果**  
我们对比测试了三种先进的算法：scHPL、treeArches和CellHint。在5个模拟场景及5个真实世界场景中，我们对这些算法在不同细胞类型与器官上的表现进行了评估。为了衡量这些算法在协调标注信息方面的效果，我们设计了三个评价指标：标注一致性F1分数（AH-F1）、树结构编辑距离相似度（TEDS）以及父子分支相似度（PCBS），并将这些算法构建的细胞类型层次结构与基于知识库建立的层次结构进行了对比。测试结果表明，这些算法在模拟数据中的表现较为优异，但在处理复杂的真实世界数据时仍存在改进空间。因此，我们开发了OTHarmonizer这一工具——该工具基于部分最优传输理论，能够高效地协调不同数据集中的细胞类型标注信息，并构建出准确的层次结构。

all_papers.title: LoMuS: Low-Rank Adaptation with Sequence Multi-representation Improves Protein Stability Prediction
all_papers.summary: Abstract Motivation Protein folding stability is a key determinant for understanding protein dynamics, including molecular function, pathogenicity, and protein engineering. Yet, accurate prediction of protein stability remains challenging due to high variability in available data, particularly when only sequence information is available and structural knowledge is limited or unavailable. In this work, we introduce LoMuS, a multi-representation-based deep learning model that predicts dataset-provided protein stability scores directly from the primary sequence. In the core of the model architecture, a fusion network integrates explicit physicochemical descriptors with low-rank adapted protein language model derived embeddings from the sequence that consistently gains across standard experimental stability benchmarks. Results We rigorously evaluate LoMuS across multiple settings, such as absolute folding stability scoring, mutation landscape stability scoring, held-out protein domains, out-of-distribution label regimes, and per-protein evaluation. LoMuS consistently outperforms sequence-only baselines, achieving an absolute performance gain of at least 10% in Spearman’s rank correlation across several benchmarks. Per-protein evaluations further demonstrate robust performance gains. Ablation analyses confirm that complementary signals from physicochemical descriptors and sequence embeddings are critical to the effectiveness of the proposed multi-representation approach. We believe LoMuS advances protein engineering research by improving the prediction and ranking of protein stability scores. Availability All codes including data preparation scripts, training and validation recipes, and experimental configurations for LoMuS are available at: https://github.com/kabir-ai2bio-lab/LoMuS

all_papers.llm_rss_summary_zh:
**摘要与动机**  
蛋白质的折叠稳定性是理解其动态行为、分子功能、致病性以及进行蛋白质工程设计的关键因素。然而，由于现有数据存在较大变异性——尤其是在仅掌握序列信息而结构信息有限或无法获取的情况下——准确预测蛋白质稳定性仍然面临挑战。在本研究中，我们提出了LoMuS这一基于多表示学习的深度学习模型，该模型能够直接根据蛋白质的初级序列来预测实验测得的稳定性数值。在模型架构的核心部分，融合网络将明确的物理化学描述符与从序列中提取的低维嵌入信息相结合，而这些嵌入信息在各种标准的稳定性评估指标中均表现出优异的性能。  

**实验结果**  
我们通过多种测试场景对LoMuS进行了严格评估，包括绝对折叠稳定性评分、突变位点对稳定性的影响分析、针对特定蛋白质结构域的预测能力测试，以及在不同数据分布条件下的性能表现。结果表明，LoMuS在各项测试中均显著优于仅依赖序列信息的传统模型，在多个评估指标上的性能提升幅度至少达到了10%。进一步的研究还证实，物理化学描述符与序列嵌入信息之间的互补作用是该模型高效预测蛋白质稳定性的关键因素。我们相信，LoMuS的问世将为蛋白质工程研究带来重要进展。

all_papers.title: UniCoracle: Automated hierarchical Feature Selection via Bottom-Up Propagation and Top-Down Skimming using the UniCorP algorithm and the Coracle machine-learning framework
all_papers.summary: Abstract Identifying meaningful associations between microbial communities and measured physiological or environmental variables becomes increasingly complex and computationally demanding given the continuous growth of microbiome datasets. The Coracle machine learning (ML) framework was recently developed to address this by integrating multiple data transformations, feature selection techniques, and ML models to yield condensed lists of features that align to target variables of interest. Further, we recently developed the UniCorP feature aggregation algorithm to identify uniquely correlated features (UNICORNs) based on the UniCor metric that iteratively enrich each taxonomic level in an automated bottom-up approach. Here we present UniCoracle, a fully automated analytical framework that integrates UniCorP’s bottom-up propagation approach with a subsequent and newly developed top-down skimming (TDS) strategy, implemented with the Coracle ML framework. This combined approach leverages the inherent taxonomic structure of microbiome community data (e.g., ASVs derived from 16S rRNA gene amplicon sequencing) to maintain predictive stability, reduce computational runtime, and identify biologically meaningful taxonomic associations. We compare the original, non-hierarchical Coracle with the TDS Coracle method and the UniCoracle approach. Evaluations across the tested datasets show that UniCoracle achieves competitive or improved predictive performance relative to both Coracle’s multi-step and the TDS-based Coracle implementations. Our results demonstrate UniCoracle’s improvements in predictive accuracy over both Coracle’s multi-step and the TDS Coracle methods. UniCoracle provides full control over feature set size and runtime, offering a streamlined and user-friendly framework for biological hypothesis generation. It identifies features (e.g., bacterial taxa) at the lowest (most specific) hierarchical level (e.g., ASV or species within a taxonomic hierarchy) that are associated with continuous target variables. Availability: UniCoracle is freely accessible via a dedicated web server at micportal.org. The source code is open-source and available on GitHub at github.com/SebastianStaab/UniCoracle.git and Zenodo at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.19050205

all_papers.llm_research_question_zh: 随着微生物组数据集的持续增长，确定微生物群落与各种生理或环境变量之间的有意义关联变得越来越复杂，同时也需要耗费更多的计算资源。
llm_highlights_zh: 最近，人们开发了Coracle机器学习框架来解决这一问题。该框架通过整合多种数据转换方法、特征选择技术以及机器学习模型，能够生成与目标变量相匹配的精简特征列表。
此外，我们最近开发了UniCorP特征聚合算法，该算法基于UniCor指标来识别那些具有独特关联性的特征，并通过自下而上的自动化方法逐步丰富各个分类层次的特征信息。
在这里，我们介绍UniCoracle——这一完全自动化的分析框架。它将UniCorP的自下而上的传播算法与随后新开发的自上而下的扫描策略相结合，并通过Coracle机器学习框架得以实现。
all_papers.llm_rss_summary_zh: 摘要：随着微生物组数据集规模的持续增长，识别微生物群落与生理或环境变量之间的关联变得越来越复杂，同时也对计算资源提出了更高的要求。为此，我们最近开发了Coracle机器学习框架——该框架通过整合多种数据转换技术、特征选择方法及机器学习模型，能够生成与目标变量相匹配的特征列表。此外，我们还设计了UniCorP特征聚合算法，该算法基于“UniCor”指标，采用自下而上的迭代方式来识别那些具有独特相关性的特征。本文所介绍的UniCoracle是一个完全自动化的分析框架：它将UniCorP的自下而上分析方法与后来开发的自上而下的筛选策略相结合，并通过Coracle机器学习框架加以实现。这种结合方式充分利用了微生物组数据本身的分类结构（例如通过16S rRNA基因扩增子测序获得的ASV信息），从而确保预测结果的稳定性、降低计算成本，并帮助识别具有生物学意义的分类关联。通过对多个测试数据集的评估，我们发现UniCoracle在预测性能上优于传统的多步骤分析方法或基于TDS策略的分析方案；其结果进一步证明了UniCoracle在预测准确性方面的优势。该框架允许用户完全控制特征集的大小及计算耗时，为生物假设的生成提供了高效且易于使用的工具。它能够识别出那些与连续型目标变量存在关联的特征——这些特征通常位于分类体系的最低层级（例如ASV或特定物种）。UniCoracle可通过micportal.org网站免费获取；其源代码已开源，可在GitHub（github.com/SebastianStaab/UniCoracle.git）及Zenodo平台（https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.19050205）上下载。

all_papers.title: Structural-information Guided Fusion for spatial domain identification from Spatial Transcriptomics
all_papers.summary: Abstract Motivation Accurate spatial domain identification is essential for understanding tissue organization and pathological mechanisms in spatial transcriptomics. However, existing methods mainly rely on expression profiles and spatial coordinates. Intercellular interactions are often overlooked. At the same time, preserving both local neighborhood continuity and global topological structure remains difficult. Results We propose SGFST (Structural-information Guided Fusion for spatial domain identification from Spatial Transcriptomics), a novel framework for spatial domain identification in spatial transcriptomics. SGFST integrates a spatial graph and a signal graph, and employs a dual-branch graph convolutional network with attention-based fusion to capture complementary spatial and functional information. In addition, SGFST jointly optimizes a Bayesian personalized ranking loss, a zero-inflated negative binomial loss, and a distance structural information constraint to preserve local neighborhood continuity, reconstruct expression signals, and maintain global topological consistency. Experimental results on multiple datasets demonstrate that SGFST outperforms several state-of-the-art methods in spatial domain identification. Availability and implementation The code of SGFST is available at Github ( https://github.com/xkmaxidian/SGFST ) and Zenodo(DOI : 10.5281/zenodo.20624899)

all_papers.llm_rss_summary_zh:
**摘要**  
在空间转录组学中，准确识别组织结构与病理机制所依赖的空间域信息至关重要。然而现有方法主要依赖于表达谱数据及空间坐标信息，往往忽视了细胞间的相互作用；同时，在保持局部邻域连续性与全局拓扑结构之间的平衡也面临挑战。  

**研究结果**  
我们提出了SGFST这一新型框架，用于解决空间转录组学中的空间域识别问题。该框架整合了空间图与信号图，并采用基于注意力机制的双分支图卷积网络来融合这两种信息，从而有效捕捉空间与功能层面的互补特征。此外，SGFST还结合了贝叶斯个性化排序损失函数、零膨胀负二项式损失函数以及距离结构信息约束条件，以同时实现局部邻域连续性的保持、表达信号的重建以及全局拓扑结构的统一性。多项实验数据表明，SGFST在空间域识别方面的性能显著优于现有先进方法。  

**代码与资源**  
SGFST的源代码可在Github（https://github.com/xkmaxidian/SGFST）及Zenodo平台（DOI：10.5281/zenodo.20624899）上获取。

all_papers.primary_summary_raw: Accurate spatial domain identification is essential for understanding tissue organization and pathological mechanisms in spatial transcriptomics. However, existing methods mainly rely on expression profiles and spatial coordinates. Intercellular interactions are often overlooked. At the same time, preserving both local neighborhood continuity and global topological structure remains difficult. Results We propose SGFST (Structural-information Guided Fusion for spatial domain identification from Spatial Transcriptomics), a novel framework for spatial domain identification in spatial transcriptomics. SGFST integrates a spatial graph and a signal graph, and employs a dual-branch graph convolutional network with attention-based fusion to capture complementary spatial and functional information. In addition, SGFST jointly optimizes a Bayesian personalized ranking loss, a zero-inflated negative binomial loss, and a distance structural information constraint to preserve local neighborhood continuity, reconstruct expression signals, and maintain global topological consistency. Experimental results on multiple datasets demonstrate that SGFST outperforms several state-of-the-art methods in spatial domain identification.

all_papers.title: ReGAIN: A bioinformatics platform for assessing probabilistic co-occurrence between resistance genes in bacterial pathogens
all_papers.summary: Abstract Motivation Multidrug-resistant bacterial pathogens continue to rise globally, yet scalable methods are needed to infer how resistance determinants co-occur across pathogen populations and to quantify conditional dependencies underlying co-occurrence and shared genetic context. Results We present ReGAIN (Resistance Gene Association and Inference Network), an open-source framework that applies Bayesian network structure learning to infer probabilistic, conditional dependency relationships among antibiotic resistance, heavy metal tolerance, stress response, and virulence determinants in bacteria. In contrast to pairwise co-occurrence analyses, ReGAIN reports conditional probabilities, relative risks, and absolute risk differences with confidence intervals to prioritize candidate relationships for downstream prioritization. Applied across ESKAPEE pathogens, ReGAIN recapitulated established resistance gene relationships and identified additional candidate patterns consistent with co-selection and shared genetic context. Together, these results support scalable, reproducible population-wide analysis of resistance networks for surveillance, comparative genomics and epidemiology. Availability ReGAIN analyses are performed using Python v3.11.5 and R v4.4.1 and is available as open-source software through Bioconda at {{ https://anaconda.org/bioconda/regain-cli }}. Source code and documentation can be found at {{ https://github.com/ERBringHorvath/regain_CLI }}. All genomes used in this publication were downloaded from the National Center for Biotechnology Information database. Large supplementary tables and results data from the ESKAPEE pathogen example network analyses can be downloaded from https://figshare.com/articles/dataset/ReGAIN_command_line_software_and_supplemental_figures_/28959431

all_papers.llm_rss_summary_zh:
**摘要**  
多重耐药细菌病原体在全球范围内持续增加，因此亟需可行的方法来研究这些耐药性决定因子在病原体群体中的共现规律，并量化其共现现象背后的条件依赖关系及共同遗传背景。  

**研究结果**  
我们开发了ReGAIN（耐药基因关联与推断网络）这一开源框架，该框架运用贝叶斯网络结构学习技术，来分析细菌中抗生素耐药性、重金属耐受性、应激反应机制以及毒力决定因子之间的概率条件依赖关系。与传统基于成对数据共现的分析方法不同，ReGAIN能够提供条件概率、相对风险及绝对风险差异，并附带置信区间，从而帮助研究人员优先筛选出具有实际研究价值的基因关联模式。在针对ESKAPEE病原体的应用中，ReGAIN不仅验证了已知的耐药基因关联关系，还发现了更多符合共同选择机制及共享遗传背景的候选基因组合。这些结果为开展大规模、可重复的群体水平耐药性网络分析提供了有力支持，有助于实现疾病监测、比较基因组学研究及流行病学分析等目标。  

**软件可用性**  
ReGAIN的分析功能可通过Python v3.11.5和R v4.4.1实现，其开源代码及使用文档可访问[[https://github.com/ERBringHorvath/regain_cli]]获取。本研究所使用的所有基因组数据均来源于美国国家生物技术信息中心数据库；而ESKAPEE病原体相关分析的补充数据则可通过[[https://figshare.com/articles/dataset/ReGAIN_command_line_software_and_supplemental_figures_/28959431]]下载。

all_papers.title: Cross-dataset annotation harmonization for cell-type hierarchy construction
all_papers.summary: Abstract Motivation Single-cell transcriptomic datasets annotate cell types with diverse schemes and varying resolution. This poses challenges in building unified hierarchical cell-type structures and hinders integration of large-scale datasets. To address this, several computational methods have been developed to harmonize cell type annotations across datasets and build data-driven hierarchies of cell types. Results Here, we benchmarked three state-of-the-art methods: scHPL, treeArches and CellHint. We evaluated these methods across 5 simulated scenarios and 5 real-world scenarios across cell types and organs. To assess harmonization results, we designed three metrics, Annotation Harmonization F1-score (AH-F1), Tree Edit Distance Similarity (TEDS) and Parent-Children Branches Similarity (PCBS), comparing the constructed cell-type hierarchies and the knowledge-based ones. Based on the benchmarking results, we found that methods performed well in simulated scenarios but still have room for improvement in complex real-world data. Thus, we developed OTHarmonizer, a tool based on partial optimal transport (OT) for cell-type harmonization and hierarchy construction. OTHarmonizer excels in accurately capturing equivalent and hierarchical relationships between cell types, offering a more effective approach for the cell-type hierarchy construction across datasets. Availability and Implementation The simulated and real-world datasets in the benchmark are available on https://figshare.com/articles/dataset/OTHarmonizer/28243205 . The source codes for the benchmark and OTHarmonizer are available online on GitHub at https://github.com/Duck-Boss/OTHarmonizer

all_papers.llm_rss_summary_zh:
**摘要与动机**  
单细胞转录组数据集采用多种不同的方案对细胞类型进行标注，且这些方案的分辨率各不相同。这种差异给构建统一的细胞类型层次结构带来了挑战，也阻碍了大规模数据集的整合与应用。为解决这一问题，人们开发了一系列计算方法，旨在协调不同数据集中的细胞类型标注信息，并建立基于数据的细胞类型层次体系。  

**研究结果**  
我们对比测试了三种先进的算法：scHPL、treeArches和CellHint。在5个模拟场景及5个真实世界场景中，我们对这些算法在不同细胞类型与器官上的表现进行了评估。为了衡量这些算法在协调标注信息方面的效果，我们设计了三个评价指标：标注一致性F1分数（AH-F1）、树结构编辑距离相似度（TEDS）以及父子分支相似度（PCBS），并将这些算法构建的细胞类型层次结构与基于知识库建立的层次结构进行了对比。测试结果表明，这些算法在模拟数据中的表现较为优异，但在处理复杂的真实世界数据时仍存在改进空间。因此，我们开发了OTHarmonizer这一工具——该工具基于部分最优传输理论，能够高效地协调不同数据集中的细胞类型标注信息，并构建出准确的层次结构。  

**数据与实现方式**  
用于测试的模拟数据集及真实世界数据集可访问地址为：https://figshare.com/articles/dataset/OTHarmonizer/28243205。本次研究的源代码可在GitHub上获取，链接为：https://github.com/Duck-Boss/OTHarmonizer
